plants.sentence: The model's power plants can make 11.6 GW more at this load level before the state stops exporting; keeping a 15 % planning reserve on the whole load, new campuses included, leaves 4.3 GW for new load.

ratings.note: The build step gave a rating to every line or transformer the dataset rates 0 ("unlimited"): its voltage class's default or 30 % above its base flow, whichever is larger.

overloaded.label: the Live Oak 7 to Live Oak 6 line
the Live Oak 7 to Live Oak 6 line

n1.method: Every line and transformer of 100 kV and up is taken out once: with the headline's 7 campuses and their upgrades connected, with all 17 of the search and theirs, and with no campus (the model's own baseline). Flows after each outage come from line outage distribution factors on the network's own factorization (DC power flow; the plants keep their output); a line or transformer is a problem past 115 % of its rating (an assumed emergency rating: the dataset gives one rating). Outages that cut off load are skipped, as the model would strand it on its own. One that cuts off only a plant moves its output to the other plants when they have the room; when they don't, it is a problem of its own (short of generation: the state would have to stop exporting or cut customers). The counts are outages, not overloads: one outage can push several lines past their rating.
n1.sentence: Single-outage screen (N-1) of 2,822 outages, with the headline's 7 campuses and their upgrades: 92 single outages push a line or transformer past 115 % of its rating where the model alone doesn't, or push it further (the model alone has 94 outages that push something past 115 %). With all 17 campuses of the search: 128 single outages push a line or transformer past 115 % of its rating where the model alone doesn't, or push it further; in 194 more, the other plants can't make up the output of a plant the outage cuts off (194 of them would cut customers, up to 1,954 MW).

rows.label: As shipped
rows.detail: The engine's dispatch: past what the plants make in the dataset, the next MW comes from their spare room.

rows.label: Dispatch pro rata to output
rows.detail: The next MW comes from every plant in proportion to what it already makes, not its spare room (the same total capacity).

rows.label: A 90 % planning limit
rows.detail: No line or transformer past 90 % of its rating (upgrades sized to carry the flow at that share).

rows.label: Estimated ratings doubled
rows.detail: The 644 ratings the build step made up (the dataset gives none) at twice their value: the optimistic side.

rows.label: Estimated ratings tighter
rows.detail: The same 644 ratings with half their room above the flow they carry today: the pessimistic side.

binds_every_case.label: the Winter Park to Orlando line

sensitivity.binds_rule: a line or transformer binds in a case when it stops a campus or the plan raises it; early: for one of its first 3 paid campuses
sensitivity.note: Each case re-runs the always-on search on a copy of the model; the headline is the shipped case.

capacity.method: Campuses go in one at a time, each where it fits with every campus so far (an exact power-flow solve). When none fits, the 30 sites closest to fitting are each solved with the campus there, the lines it would push past their rating are raised to a standard level and priced, and the cheapest bundle is built. With every line in service (N-0), the final set runs through the cascade engine: nothing trips. That checks N-0 only; a single-outage (N-1) screen of the headline's campuses follows. Flexible campuses must fit twice: at full size at 90 % of this load, and at half size at it.

ai.reason: Replacing Land O Lakes with Haines City reduces local flows sufficiently to avoid all five line rebuilds while keeping seven campuses.

trace.title: Sent Gemini the engine's plan: seven campuses at once for $36.6M
trace.detail: Asked for one more campus for no more than that, or the same seven for less (the engine's plan needs $60.5M for eight). Also sent: what each of its campuses and 39 other candidate sites put on the lines that matter (a distribution-factor table), the raises a moved campus could save, each line's price, the weak points and the plants' room.

trace.title: Proposed: an eighth campus at Haines City
trace.detail: In its words: “Replacing Land O Lakes with Haines City adds an eighth campus while avoiding marginal line overloads and eliminating expensive Orlando line rebuilds.” Eight campuses (new: Haines City); raises Orlando 54 transformer to 850 MVA, Jacksonville 64 transformer to 600 MVA and Mulberry 3–1 line to 300 MVA and 1 more.

trace.title: Engine solved all eight campuses at once: 12 lines over their rating
trace.detail: Over: Orlando 27–54 line at 120 % of 92 MVA; Orlando 54–20 line (circuit 1) at 110 % of 148 MVA (+10 more). Priced by the engine: $33.9M (high end; Gemini's own numbers are not used).

trace.title: Sent the engine's findings back to Gemini
trace.detail: The 12 lines over their rating and by how much, the raise each needs and its price; what the plan really costs ($33.9M) against the bar. Asked for one revised plan.

trace.title: Revised: seven campuses with one moved to Haines City
trace.detail: In its words: “Replacing Land O Lakes with Haines City reduces local flows sufficiently to avoid all five line rebuilds while keeping seven campuses.” Seven campuses (new: Haines City; dropped: Land O Lakes); raises Orlando 54 transformer to 800 MVA, Jacksonville 64 transformer to 550 MVA and Gainesville 34 transformer to 150 MVA.

trace.title: Engine solved all seven campuses at once: five lines over their rating
trace.detail: Over: Orlando 27–54 line at 105 % of 92 MVA; Orlando 54–20 line (circuit 1) at 104 % of 148 MVA (+3 more). Priced by the engine: $28.5M (high end; Gemini's own numbers are not used). Sized up by the engine's 10 % margin rule: Jacksonville 64 transformer 550 to 600 MVA; Orlando 54 transformer 800 to 850 MVA.

trace.title: The engine's plan stands: Gemini didn't beat it
trace.detail: Only a plan the engine re-solves, prices and runs through the full cascade can count as a win. 2 rounds, 2 Gemini calls, 3.8 s.

attempts.phrase: took the Orlando 27–54 line to 120 % of its rating (11 more lines over)
took the Orlando 27–54 line to 105 % of its rating (four more lines over)

ai.sentence: Gemini's two proposals didn't beat the engine's plan: one took the Orlando 27–54 line to 120 % of its rating (11 more lines over); the other also took it to 105 % (four more lines over).
ai.rules: The engine re-solved Gemini's whole plan at once (every campus and every raise): no line or transformer past its rating that wasn't already over with no campus, no load the plants can't supply; each raise sized by the engine's own rule (the flow plus a 10 % margin, in 50 MVA steps, within 5x the original rating) and priced by the engine at the high end (Gemini's own figures are not used); then the full cascade: nothing may trip.

result.cost_basis: Each upgrade priced with published figures: re-conductoring (low) or a rebuild (high) per mile at the line's voltage class, a new line past twice the rating, and $ per MVA for transformers (Black & Veatch 2014, CPI-adjusted to 2024 $). Ranked and totaled at the high end.
